web.description:
# Meet the African startups that raised funding in July 2026
In H1 2026, African startups raised $1.44 billion through 146 deals, slightly more than the $1.42 billion raised in the same period of 2025, but with fewer overall deals (252 last year).

![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/4f0dba0e1af7914c81749b91a5bf568f0407ea2a7eebe8692693080b7b4644dd?s=36&d=mm&r=g)

## Vigneshwar
Copy link to article

![](https://african-startups.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Meet-the-African-startups-that-raised-funding-in-July-2026-1024x576.jpg)

_Editor’s note: [**African-Startups**](http://african-startups.com/) is a sister publication of [**EU-Startups**](https://www.eu-startups.com/), bringing trusted coverage of startups, venture capital, and innovation across Africa_.

July 2026 was a busy month for African startups raising capital, with deals spanning from FinTech, HealthTech, to food processing and EdTech across more than a dozen markets.

The funding varied from six-figure grants to eight-figure investments, with a diverse range of investors including pan-African venture funds, impact investors, and much more.

In H1 2026, African startups [raised](https://african-startups.com/know-how/african-startups-raised-1-44-billion-in-h1-2026-with-ev-startup-spiro-securing-the-single-biggest-deal/) $1.44 billion through 146 deals, slightly more than the $1.42 billion raised in the same period of 2025, but with fewer overall deals (252 last year).

A significant portion of the funding went to just seven companies, with Spiro leading at $320 million.

Debt financing increased by 37% year-on-year, rising from $448 million in H1 2025 to $614 million in H1 2026, as startups opted for debt to grow without giving up equity.

The World Bank’s Africa Economic Update [says](https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/afr/publication/africa-economic-update) that the growth in sub-Saharan Africa is projected to hold at 4.1% in 2026, unchanged from 2025, with projections revised downward by 0.3 percentage points from October 2025 estimates.

Even though the total value of new greenfield projects dropped by nearly a third, the number of projects actually went up, says the report.

As a result, more investors are participating with smaller investments, despite the challenging global conditions.

More investors are making smaller, focused investments across the continent, similar to trends in the startup scene, where money is being directed to fewer, but stronger companies.

Having said that, here are the startups that closed funding rounds in July 2026.

## ORA Technologies
Funding in July 2026: [$2 million Series A extension](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/moroccan-super-app-ora-technologies-raises-2-million-taking-series-a-funding-to-10-million/)

Total funding since inception now sits at nearly $12 million. Azur Innovation Fund led the extension round alongside other Moroccan private investors.

## Built Financial Technologies
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

It is a 10-year-old FinTech company that helps small businesses handle accounting, payroll, invoicing, payments, and inventory from one place. Total funding to date stands at $365k. Backed through Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, a $4 million pilot vehicle funded by FMO and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency.

## GrowForMe
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

GrowForMe is an AgTech platform that connects farmers, aggregators, and buyers through input financing, warehousing, and commodity trading. GrowForMe says it has worked with more than 19,000 farmers and facilitated over $3.9 million in trade since launch. Earlier backers include Google’s Black Founders Fund, develoPPP Ventures, and the UN Capital Development Fund. Backed through Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility.

## Mathesis Analytics
Funding in July 2026: Undisclosed

HQ: Nigeria

Founded by Winston Osuchukwu, Mathesis Analytics aims to improve credit access in Africa. Mathesis solves this with “Personal Equity,” a system that compiles a person’s financial behaviour into a single, portable credit identity. So far, it has helped provide over eight million loans to more than two million borrowers in Nigeria. The company received investment from First Ally Capital to expand its operations across Africa.

## Lemonade Payments
Funding in July 2026: [Undisclosed](https://african-startups.com/countries/kenya/kenyan-fintech-startup-lemonade-payments-lands-plug-and-play-backing-to-scale-payment-infrastructure-across-africa/)

Founded in 2023 by Mark Machiri Kihara and Andrew Kibe, Lemonade Payments lets people send, receive, and manage money without exposing their personal details during the transaction. Baobab Network invested first in Lemonade with a $100k cheque in 2024, and Plug and Play Ventures, the venture arm of the Silicon Valley innovation platform, has now joined the cap table as the company pushes into new African markets.

# African startups hit $2.10 billion in 8 months
##### Published 4th SEPTEMBER 2026
African startups raised $2.10B across 275 deals in the first 8 months of 2026. Read our analysis of August's $438M surge, mega-deals, and early-stage grants.

Between January and August 2026, African startups raised $2.10 billion across 275 tracked funding deals, slightly edging out the $2.07 billion raised during the same eight-month period in 2025.

However, month-on-month activity fluctuated significantly, driven by massive spikes in February ($361.7M), June ($334.7M), and August ($438.0M) which surged by 209%, 56%, and 368% respectively over their 2025 monthly baselines.

## Top markets and mega-deals
Nigeria leads the continent in capital attraction so far in 2026, pulling in $528.6 million.

## August 2026 performance: Moove, e-commerce, and crypto lead $438 million Surge
August 2026 recorded an impressive $438.01 million in total funding, driven by large growth rounds and strategic debt facilities.

![](https://insights.techcabal.com/wp-content/uploads/insight/2026/09/Africas-top-funded-startups-in-August-2026-819x1024.jpg)

- Naran raised $10 million in debt and equity from Landel.
- ThriveAgric raised a [$3.93 million](https://techcabal.com/zu/2026/08/25/thriveagric-commercial-paper-raise-5-3-billion-naira/) debt facility.

# Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M [2026]
![Laura Bennett](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/lbennett.webp)

Updated Oct 23, 2026 · 17 min read

[Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2Fnigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026%2F&text=Nigeria%20Tops%20Africa%20Startup%20Funding%20at%20%24635M%20%5B2026%5D)[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2Fnigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026%2F)[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2Fnigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026%2F)[Share on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2Fnigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026%2F&title=Nigeria%20Tops%20Africa%20Startup%20Funding%20at%20%24635M%20%5B2026%5D)[Copy link](https://shattered.io/nigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026/)

![Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026-gen-1024x585.webp)

Nigerian startups raised **$635 million** between January and September 2026, according to data from the tracker Africa: The Big Deal, and that total puts Nigeria back at the top of the continent’s startup-funding table. [BusinessDay reported](https://businessday.ng/technology/article/nigeria-reclaims-africas-startup-funding-lead-as-investment-hits-635m/) that the result is Nigeria’s first lead in African startup funding since 2022. Reports published on October 21 put the figure at 2.6 times the $247 million Nigerian startups raised in the same nine months of 2025.

A total of 77 Nigerian ventures raised funding in the period, up from 70 a year earlier.

![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)·

[Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F)

## Nigeria Startup Funding Versus 2025: 2.6 Times the Money
Nigerian startups raised $247 million in January through September 2025 and $635 million in the same window of 2026. That is an increase of $388 million, or about 157%. [Nairametrics framed the result](https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/21/nigeria-reclaims-africas-startup-funding-lead-as-investments-rise-to-635-million/) as a rise in investment to $635 million, and several other Nigerian outlets used near-identical language on October 21.

| Metric (Jan-Sep) | 2025 | 2026 | Change |
|-|-|-|-|
| Funding raised by Nigerian startups | $247 million | $635 million | 2.6x (about +157%) |
| Ventures raising $100K or more | 70 | 77 | +7 (+10%) |
| Average raised per venture (derived) | about $3.5 million | about $8.2 million | about 2.3x |

## FAQ: Nigeria Startup Funding in 2026
### How much did Nigerian startups raise in the first nine months of 2026?
Nigerian startups raised $635 million between January and September 2026, according to Africa: The Big Deal data cited by Nigerian and African outlets. Reports published on October 21 gave the figure.

### How does that compare with 2025?
The 2026 total is 2.6 times the $247 million raised in the same period of 2025. The number of ventures raising at least $100,000 rose from 70 to 77.

### How much did all of Africa raise?
African startups collectively raised approximately $2.16 billion between January and September 2026.

### What does Africa: The Big Deal track?
The tracker monitors African startups that raise at least $100,000.

# August 2026: Mo(o)ving up
### Moove and a handful of large deals really moved the needle in August, while lower-value tickets lagged
In August 2026, 31 start-ups in Africa announced funding rounds of $100k or more, raising a combined $455m (excluding exits).

At the top was [Moove](https://thebigdeal.substack.com/p/unimoove): the Nigerian-born mobility company’s $250m Series C alone represented 55% of all the funding. [Jumia raised $50m](https://group.jumia.com/news/jumia-wins-ifc-axian-backing-in-50-million-equity-fundraising-bloomberg) in equity, [Yellow Card $40m](https://yellowcard.io/blog/yellow-card-secures-40-million-in-strategic-funding-to-further-global-expansion), [Moment $22m](https://www.africatechsummit.com/insights/moment-raises-22m-series-a-to-accelerate-africas-most-comprehensive-payments-and-billing-platform/), and ValU completed a [$21m corporate bond issuance](https://www.efgholding.com/en/media/news/Valu1stCorporateBond). The Big Four captured almost everything: 99.5% of the amount raised and 94% of $100k+ deals (29 out of 31); Nigeria alone accounted for $364m, or 80% of all funding raised.

From January to August, African start-ups have now raised $1.92b, only 9% below the same period in 2025. Equity is actually up 23% YoY, at $1.35b, thanks largely to the two mega-rounds from Spiro and Moove.

web.description:
According to [Crunchbase published in July of 2026](https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=93740), Global startups raised a record $510 billion in the first half of 2026 alone.

## Global Startup Funding by Region
Series A funding across the region grew 10 percent from 2024 to 2025, then accelerated further into 2026, with Q1 2026 Series A funding running 56 percent higher than the 2025 quarterly average.

## Africa’s Startup Funding Story: A Real Comeback, With Caveats
That is a 25 percent increase from the $3.25 billion raised in 2024, and the strongest single-year total since the 2022 peak of $6.5 billion.

African tech startups raised a record $1.64 billion in debt financing in 2025, a 63 percent increase from the year before and the highest level ever recorded on the continent.

Disrupt Africa’s 11th annual report, meanwhile, counted only equity funding and arrived at $1.64 billion across 178 startups, a 46.2 percent increase from 2024’s $1.12 billion.

Partech’s data shows Series A rounds up 21 percent and Series B rounds up 12 percent in average size during 2025, even though the number of deals barely changed.

## Which African Countries Are Leading?
The country raised $1.04 billion in total funding, a 72 percent jump from 2024, making it the top destination for African startup capital for the first time in years.

## Conclusion
$4.1 billion raised in 2025 marks real recovery after two difficult years, and the shift toward debt financing shows a growing number of African startups have reached the kind of operational maturity that makes them creditworthy, not just fundable.

# Logistics Attracts $780 Million, Overtaking Fintech in African Startup Funding
- **African logistics and transport startups raised $780 million between January and September 2026, ahead of fintech, which attracted $760 million.**
- **African startups raised $2.16 billion in the first nine months of 2026, down about 4% from $2.24 billion a year earlier, while Nigeria led country rankings with $635 million.**

African logistics and transport startups raised $780 million between January and September 2026, surpassing fintech's $760 million, according to data published on Tuesday, October 20, by Africa: The Big Deal.

Electric motorcycle company Spiro raised $345 million, while Moove, which finances vehicles for drivers working with mobility platforms, secured $250 million.

Together, the two companies raised $595 million, representing about 76% of the funding attributed to logistics and transport during the first nine months of the year.

At least 80 fintech companies each raised $100,000 or more between January and September 2026, according to Africa: The Big Deal.

African startups raised $2.16 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $2.24 billion over the same period in 2025, representing a decrease of about 4%.

Nigeria attracted $635 million in startup funding between January and September 2026, placing it ahead of Egypt, which secured $445 million.
